content:
incident-bot: Pager alert triggered for genqueue errors in us-west-2 (severity: P1). Error rate spike >60% for model fastgen-service. Runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/genqueue

 dylan: on it. I'll grab logs and start mitigation.

 alice: pulling logs now, will draft initial statuspage text.

 ben: thanks — tag me when you have the draft, I'll review for customer impact wording.

 carla: which customers/regions are seeing failures? Any SLA impact?

 dylan: primarily us-west-2 workers, some spillover to us-east under load. Early indicator: backpressure on the genqueue dispatcher, not model corruption. SLA at risk for tail latency; customers with reserved capacity may be unaffected.

 incident-bot: assign -> dylan (oncall)

 alice: DRAFT initial status (for review):

 "We are investigating elevated error rates and timeouts affecting text generation requests in US-West (us-west-2). Some requests may experience errors or increased latency. Engineers are actively investigating and working on mitigation."

 alice: Posting this as initial notice — thoughts?

 ben: small wording tweak: replace "text generation" with "model inference requests" and add "affecting a subset of customers".

 alice: updated draft:

 "We are investigating elevated error rates and timeouts affecting model inference requests in US-West (us-west-2). A subset of customers may see errors or increased latency. Engineers are actively investigating and working on mitigation."

 carla: add estimated customer impact: "Most customers unaffected; customers with high-concurrency genqueue usage may be impacted." Also request ETA placeholder.

 emma: mitigation update — we're throttling new batch dispatches and spinning an isolated worker to take traffic. ETA for first reduction in errors ~10m. Add that.

 alice: updated draft with mitigation and ETA:

 "We are investigating elevated error rates and timeouts affecting model inference requests in US-West (us-west-2). A subset of customers may see errors or increased latency. Engineers are throttling new batch dispatches and provisioning additional worker capacity; we expect initial improvement within ~10 minutes. We will provide updates every 15 minutes or as the situation changes."

 ben: approve with :thumbsup: — can publish initial.

 dylan: publishing initial to status page now.

 incident-bot: statuspage.update: initial -> Published by dylan

 alice: thanks. I'll monitor logs and prepare first periodic update.

 --- 12 minutes later ---

 dylan: UPDATE 1: error rate reduced ~40% after throttling and new worker. Some residual 5xx for long-tail requests. Continuing to scale and investigate dispatcher backlog.

 carla: can we include affected endpoints list? (generation, streaming)

 alice: added affected endpoints line in update:

 "Affected services: /v1/generate, /v1/streaming (subset of requests)."

 ben: add note re: dedicated customers: "Dedicated capacity customers: minimal impact. If you notice otherwise, reach out to support."

 emma: currently gathering heap profiles and dispatcher metrics; will post findings in 10m.

 dylan: UPDATE 2 (periodic): we've cleared most backpressure; error rate back to ~5% above baseline. Root cause likely a rare dispatcher scheduling path that created a hot queue. Rolling mitigation deployed to route around the hot slot. Continuing to watch.

 alice: preparing resolved notice draft.

 alice: RESOLVED DRAFT:

 "Resolved — The elevated error rates and timeouts affecting model inference in US-West (us-west-2) have been mitigated. Engineers deployed a routing fix to bypass a dispatcher hot slot and scaled worker capacity; service metrics are returning to normal. If you continue to see issues, please contact support with request IDs."

 carla: small tweak: add timeline (start/end) and note about root cause investigation ongoing.

 alice: final resolved draft:

 "Resolved — Between 14:08 and 14:32 UTC we observed elevated error rates and timeouts for model inference requests in US-West (us-west-2). Engineers deployed a routing fix and scaled worker capacity; service metrics have returned to normal. We are continuing an investigation into the dispatcher scheduling path that caused a hot queue. If you continue to experience issues, please contact support with request IDs."

 ben: LGTM. :white_check_mark:

 dylan: publishing resolved notice now.

 incident-bot: statuspage.update: resolved -> Published by dylan

 emma: logging note: saved heap profiles and attached to incident ticket #INC-1897.

 dylan: closing pager, handing back to SRE for postmortem.

 incident-bot: pager resolved -> closed by dylan

 carla: thanks everyone — will start a short incident postmortem doc and link to this thread.

 alice: adding cross-links in the postmortem and customer comms templates.

 ben: good job. Keep a TODO: check dispatcher scheduling unit tests and add canary for hot-queue detection.
